name: boxd

modes.label: Pay as you go (credits, USD list)
modes.commit_note: No commitment. Custom plan offers volume pricing, but rates are not published.
modes.note: vCPU is billed on the full shape size while running. RAM is billed on RESIDENT memory, sampled per second, so ram_util stands in for resident fraction. Shapes provision 4 GiB per vCPU (1/4, 2/8, 4/16). The 4/16 shape and larger need an email to contact@boxd.sh; the self-serve max is 2 vCPU / 8 GiB. EUR list: EUR 0.049 / vCPU-h, EUR 0.015 / GiB-h. The USD list is the provider's own separate list, not an FX conversion. Basis verified 2026-09-28: "vCPU is the one component billed on the machine's size: its full vCPU count while it runs, nothing in standby, hibernated or stopped." ; "RAM bills on the memory a machine actually has resident, sampled every second, while it is running or in standby, not on the 8 GiB it was provisioned with." (https://boxd.sh/faq/). Auto-suspend: "a machine suspends after N seconds of no inbound TCP/UDP traffic"; auto-hibernate "After 4 hours of no inbound TCP/UDP traffic" (https://docs.boxd.sh/how-it-works/suspend-resume). Whether page cache counts as resident is not documented.

plans.name: Pay as you go
plans.note: Self-serve. 50 machines per org, hibernated machines included (2 without a payment method). Default shape 2 vCPU / 8 GiB / 100 GiB CoW. Prepaid credits with $20 auto top-up.

plans.name: Pay as you go (quota/shape raised on request)
plans.note: Email contact@boxd.sh; same-day approval is typical. 4 vCPU / 16 GiB shape is shown on the rate card. The raised quota level is not published.

plans.name: Custom
plans.note: Bigger machines, volume pricing, SSO + audit logs, EU residency, dedicated support, self-host or BYOC (annual licence). No published prices.

perf_source: No benchmark row: provider is not in ComputeSDK results or the HPC run (as of 2026-09-28). See research/perf-map.json.

knobs.label: Share of session running (rest hibernated)
knobs.why: boxd bills vCPU + resident RAM only while running; a hibernated machine (memory written to disk) pays written disk only. Use <1 if machines hibernate during idle gaps. Do NOT use it for standby (auto-suspend): standby drops vCPU but keeps billing resident RAM per the pricing FAQ, so it saves far less than hibernate (the docs' 'near zero' claim conflicts).

knobs.label: Idle tail before auto-hibernate (x session hours)
knobs.why: Auto-hibernate triggers only after 4 h with no network traffic (default; it watches network, not CPU). A machine left alone after its work keeps billing full vCPU + RAM for up to 4 h. Factor = (session + idle tail) / session, e.g. 1 h sessions left to auto-hibernate = 5x; the 5x max is that worst case for 1 h sessions.

caveats: Price history (v8-history audit): the 2026-05-26 archived pricing page advertised Individual EUR 20/month in its headline but 'EUR 0 forever, no credit card' in its own FAQ (team FAQ EUR 25-200/user/month); actual old invoice terms unknown. By 2026-08-31 it had moved to the current credit-metered regime (EUR 0.049/vCPU-h, EUR 0.015/used-GiB-h, EUR 0.0001/written-GiB-h, EUR 30 starting credit; live-checked 2026-09-28). A regime change, not a measurable discount; EUR->USD toggle differences are FX, not price changes.
EUR-native pricing. The USD list ($0.059 / $0.018 / $0.00012) is about 1.2x the EUR list (EUR 0.049 / 0.015 / 0.0001). EUR payers' USD cost depends on FX. Prices exclude VAT.
RAM is billed on resident memory, not the provisioned 4 GiB per vCPU. The estimate uses ram_util as the resident fraction. Whether page cache counts as resident is undocumented.

paused_ram_billed=true models STANDBY (optional auto-suspend: RAM + disk, no vCPU), per the pricing FAQ. The docs contradict this, calling standby 'near zero'. Default idle behaviour is HIBERNATE after 4 h without network traffic, which bills written disk only.

Idle timers watch network traffic, not CPU. Machines left running bill full rate for up to 4 h (the default auto-hibernate window) after traffic stops. Disabling auto-hibernate means indefinite full billing.

snapshot_gib_month uses the published written-disk rate ($0.00012 / GiB-h), which applies to hibernated or stopped machines. Standalone named snapshots, backups (object storage, 7-day default retention) and volumes have no published price.
Disk is billed on bytes written, not the 100 GiB CoW provisioned. Forks share blocks.

Egress price not published (null): the rate card bills only vCPU, resident RAM and written disk, and the egress guide covers egress control only, with no transfer price or allowance (boxd.sh/pricing + docs.boxd.sh/guides/egress rendered 2026-09-28). Not assumed free. No dedicated IPv4: machines sit behind a shared proxy IP, with 3 raw TCP/UDP forwards per machine (docs.boxd.sh/guides/resources: 'a dedicated SSH port on boxd's shared proxy IP'). Note boxd.sh/faq marketing copy says each machine has 'a public IPv4'; the docs table is followed here (verified 2026-09-28).
4 vCPU / 16 GiB and larger shapes need a request; the self-serve max is 2 vCPU / 8 GiB. No published ceiling for Custom.
min_billed_seconds=0: the vendor says 'metered every second' and publishes no minimum.
No benchmark data for boxd in benchmarks.json. The vendor claims <10 ms boot and ~85 ms wake from hibernate.

Idle suspension on boxd is two-stage: auto-suspend (standby) stops vCPU billing but keeps billing resident RAM + written disk; only hibernate (default after 4 h without inbound traffic) drops to disk only. The engine's idle auto-suspend saving (auto_stop_idle) removes whole hours and so overstates savings for short idle gaps; use running_pct / hibernate_tail instead.

The vendor's own pricing-page calculator prices standby: 'Personal assistant' = 1 h/day running at $0.1564/h + 4 h/day standby at $0.0384/h (2 GiB resident x $0.018 + 20 GiB written x $0.00012) + 19 h/day hibernated at $0.0024/h = $10.82/month (730 h month). This confirms paused_ram_billed=true on the pricing page itself; the docs still say standby costs 'near zero' (checked 2026-09-29).

Currency is fixed per organization at creation (EUR or USD list), and prepaid credit purchases/top-ups are non-refundable per the Terms (last updated 2026-05-08). An org cannot switch to whichever list is cheaper at current FX.

fleet.verification: Adding a payment card unlocks 50 machines and introductory credits; no charge just for adding card. Automatic wallet refills can charge thereafter.
fleet.tiers: New org without payment method 2; card on file 50 per organization; higher machine count/shapes by email contact@boxd.sh.
fleet.notes: Official resource guide says all listed limits can be raised and requests generally approved the same day (encoded as within 1 day, not an SLA). Hibernated retained machines count too. 10/50 supported after card; 300/1,000 need human review, not guaranteed. The 50-machine quota is per organization and a personal context counts as its own org, so one user with a personal context plus a team org has two separate 50-machine quotas (and two credit balances).

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: On by default, set to 4 hours. After 4 hours of no inbound TCP/UDP traffic, boxd hibernates the machine: a snapshot is written to disk and its memory is released.
snapshot_auto.note: Trigger: no inbound network traffic (not CPU idleness) for the auto-hibernate timeout (default 4 h, configurable, 0 = never). Memory, processes and open sockets included; wakes in ~85 ms on the next inbound packet. Optional auto-suspend (off by default) freezes the VM in host RAM after N s idle. Separate: scheduled disk backups to object storage (disaster-recovery guide), not counted here.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: A snapshot is a saved copy of a specific machine. It captures the disk and the memory, so a machine booted from the snapshot is already running whatever the original machine was running (at time of snapshotting).
snapshot_on_demand.note: Memory included. Named, versioned snapshots boot any number of new machines (`boxd machine new --from-snapshot`); machine must be running to snapshot; a machine can snapshot itself from inside. Also: checkpoints (memory+disk, up to 10 per machine, in-place restore), live fork of a running machine, manual pause/resume.

harness_api.quote: boxd machine exec myapp 'claude -p "Add a /health endpoint" --dangerously-skip-permissions'
harness_api.note: Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode are preinstalled and pre-configured (agent_harnesses), with Claude Code login synced across machines, but the documented way to drive them from outside is the generic exec API/CLI or SSH + tmux + Claude's own /remote-control. No boxd API to start a prompt, stream agent events or list/resume sessions. The Claude Managed Agents / OpenAI Agents API integrations run Anthropic's/OpenAI's harness with boxd as the tool-execution environment (worker/executor inside the VM), not a boxd harness API.

egress_allowlist.quote: Two controls, both set from the SDK and enforced outside the machine, so nothing running inside it (root included) can loosen them: An egress allowlist per machine: the hosts and addresses it may reach. Everything else is blocked.
egress_allowlist.note: Entries: exact hostnames, wildcards (*.npmjs.org; refused on shared-hosting domains), public IPv4 addresses and CIDRs. HTTP(S) admitted by hostname, other protocols by destination IP. Changes live within a second. Set via SDK/gRPC (SetVmEgressAllow) only, not the laptop CLI yet. Default: unrestricted. `--isolated` additionally cuts the machine off from your own fleet. No IPv6 egress.

egress_http_rules.quote: Entries are bare hosts and addresses: no scheme, port, or path.
egress_http_rules.note: Allowlist is host/IP only; no method/path/header rules documented. (The secret proxy does rewrite HTTPS to bound hosts, but only for placeholder substitution.)

ingress_rules.quote: Serve your whole org over your company tailnet. Same hostnames, same TLS, reachable only from inside your Tailscale network.
ingress_rules.note: By default every machine has a public HTTPS proxy name.boxd.sh -> port 8000; you choose which extra ports get subdomain proxies and up to 3 raw TCP/UDP forwards (owner-only). Tailnet-only mode is org-wide and enabled by contacting boxd; bot protection (browser check) on wake. No per-machine IP allowlist or authenticated preview URL documented.

guest_firewall.quote: Code in the sandbox can run Docker, load kernel modules, restart `systemd`, edit `/etc`, open ports, and break the OS completely
guest_firewall.note: KVM microVM with its own kernel and network stack, root inside; nftables/iptables not explicitly documented but Docker (which programs iptables) runs natively.

secret_proxy.quote: Inside the machine `STRIPE_KEY` is an opaque string starting with `bxds_`. A request to `api.stripe.com` that carries it, in a header, the query string, the body, or Basic auth, arrives at Stripe with the real key. A request anywhere else carries the useless placeholder.
secret_proxy.note: Any secret can be bound to arbitrary hosts (`domains`), org-level, applies to forks/restores. HTTPS is intercepted with a boxd CA the VM trusts (cert-pinning tools fail). HTTP(S) only; no mention of databases/SSH/git-over-SSH. Separately, unbound secrets are injected as real env vars.

volume_attach.note: Persistent disks, created writable, attachable read-write or read-only, at create time (volumes=[VolumeMount]) or later; not combinable with --from-snapshot at creation. No published price.

volume_shared.quote: For now a disk can only be attached to one VM at a time (regardless of mode) — its backing file lives on one specific worker, not shared/networked storage, so this request is rejected if the disk already has any attachment.
volume_shared.note: Local worker-backed disk, one VM at a time even read-only. Forks get CoW copies, not a shared mount.
